human: We theoretically investigate Cooper quartet correlations in doubly-magic nuclei( Ca 40 , Sn 100 , and Pb 164 ).We first examine the quartet condensation fraction in infinite symmetric nuclear matter by using the quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory.Together with the total nucleon density profiles of doubly-magic nuclei obtained from the Skyrme Hartree-Fock calculation,we discuss the spatial distribution of quartet correlations in finite nuclei within the local density approximation.Large quartet condensate fractions are found at the surface region of an atomic nucleus due to the strong neutron-proton attractive interactions responsible for the deuteron formation in vacuum.Moreover, we discuss a possible microscopic origin of the Wigner term in the context of nucleon-quartet scattering in dilute symmetric nuclear matter.The nucleon-quartet scattering effect on the Wigner term is numerically estimated as about one order of magnitude of the total empirical strength,indicating the importance of multi-nucleon clusters in the symmetry energy and mass formula in addition to the neutron-proton pairing.
ai: Our theoretical exploration delves into Cooper quartet correlations in nuclei characterized as doubly-magic, specifically focusing on Calcium-40, Tin-100, and Lead-164. We initiate our inquiry by evaluating the quartet condensation fraction within infinite symmetric nuclear matter utilizing the quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer framework. Coupled with the comprehensive nucleon density profiles derived for doubly-magic nuclei through the Skyrme Hartree-Fock computation, this approach allows us to explore the spatial distribution of quartet correlations in finite nuclei via the local density approximation method. We observe substantial quartet condensate fractions particularly near the surface of an atomic nucleus, a phenomenon attributable to the intense neutron-proton attractive forces that facilitate deuteron formation in a vacuum. Beyond this, we delve into a potential microscopic origin for the Wigner term, examining it through the lens of nucleon-quartet interactions within dilute symmetric nuclear matter. Our numerical estimations indicate that the impact of nucleon-quartet scattering on the Wigner term approximates an entire order of magnitude when compared to the total empirical strength. This finding underscores the significant role that multi-nucleon clusters play in both the symmetry energy and the mass formula, complementing the effects of neutron-proton pairing.
